To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the guest dependent energy and safety of 3D porous MOF based energetic materials were investigated by the synthesis and characterization of thermohydrate and anhydrous forms of a 3D porous metal organic framework.

a new, stable energetic material, with the nitrogen content as high as 59.85%, was prepared from a thermohydrate reaction of the nitrogen rich ligands with the Co(II) ions, and this new material is much more sensitive than the starting material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new strategy for storage, transportation and transformation of sensitive, high energy materials.
new strategy for storage of sensitive high energy and high nitrogen materials.

a new, stable energetic material 1 and its transformation to a more energetic, sensitive material 2 with the nitrogen content and heat of denonation comparable to those of the most popular energetic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the guest dependent energy and safety of 3D MOFs is a promising new strategy for safe storage and transportation of high energy materials.
the guest dependent energy and sensitivities of 3D MOFs based energetic materials can be used to develop a novel strategy for storage and transformation of energetic materials.
the 3D MOF based materials with high nitrogen contents are more sensitive and can be used as a safe storage form for the more sensitive 3D, high nitrogen content materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the guest dependent energy and the sensitivity of 3 D, MOF based energetic materials can be controlled by the selection of suitable guests and/or by thermohydration of the energetic MOF.
the 3D MOF 1 can be used as a safe storage and transportation form for the more sensitive 2.
2 can be obtained from 1 by removing water molecules from 1, which can be regarded as an efficient way for the production of high energetic materials from low energetic ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3D, metal organic framework based, high energy materials can be produced with the desired nitrogen content and sensitivity by changing the guest.
3D MOF based energetic materials can be used to store and transport sensitive energetic compounds in less sensitive, thermohydrate form.
guest dependent energy and sensitivities of 3D MOF based energetic materials can be tuned by controlling the amount and the identity of the guest molecules.
